Mappa di avvisi e vulnerabilità sfruttat: Advisories and exploited vulnerabilities map — EVIL
Mappa didattica di avvisi di sicurezza e: An educational map of security advisories and exploited vulnerabilities from official public sources: CISA KEV, NIST NVD, CERT-AGID, CERT-EU and Cisco Talos. What is real, what is aggregated and how to read it.
Raccoglie le voci più recenti di catalog: Collects the latest entries from official catalogues and advisories: CISA KEV, NIST NVD, CERT-AGID, CERT-EU, CISA advisories and Cisco Talos research. These are vulnerabilities and advisories, not attacks in progress: the position on the map is the area of the publishing organisation, not the location of victims.
<strong>Cosa è reale.</strong> Ogni voce: What is real. Every entry comes from an official public source and links to the original page. Descriptions stay in the source’s language (usually English; Italian for CERT-AGID).
<strong>Cosa è aggregato.</strong> Un ma: What is aggregated. One marker groups all the entries published by organisations in the same area: United States (CISA, NIST), Italy (CERT-AGID), European Union (CERT-EU). Sources with no area of their own, such as Cisco Talos, are counted separately under “No geographical area”.
<strong>Cosa non è.</strong> Non mostra: What it is not. It does not show where attacks happen or who has been hit: a vulnerability published by NIST concerns products used all over the world.
<strong>Gravità.</strong> Viene dal punt: Severity. It comes from the CVSS score when the source provides one. The KEV catalogue does not assign a severity: it states that the vulnerability is actively exploited, which is exactly why it should be fixed first.

Ogni cerchio è un’area, cioè la sede deg: Each circle is an area, meaning where the publishing organisations are based; its colour shows how many entries come from it (yellow: up to 8, orange: up to 15, red: more). Click a circle or an entry in the list for details. The map is fixed, with no zoom.
Dati aggiornati, cache ed esempi: che di: Up-to-date data, cache and examples: what is the difference?
<strong>Dati aggiornati</strong> — il se: Up-to-date data — the server queries the sources every 5 minutes; the “Source status” line shows which ones responded to the last attempt.
<strong>Ultimi dati reali (cache)</stron: Last real data (cache) — if the sources do not respond, the last data downloaded stays on screen, with its time under “Updated”.
<strong>Esempi</strong> — se nessuna fon: Examples — if no source responds and there is no cache, the page shows a few example entries, labelled as such: real, well-known vulnerabilities from the KEV catalogue (not the latest ones) and a description of the type of content the other sources publish. They are not the current feed.
I numeri si riferiscono solo alle voci c: The figures refer only to the loaded entries (the latest from each source), not to all existing vulnerabilities.
